newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore property market to languish in doldrums.
newsitem.headline: Singapore property market to languish in doldrums.

text.p: The Singapore property market will suffer from a glut of unsold units and is not seen recovering anytime soon, senior officials of DBS Land said.
"We believe sentiment will continue to be weak," DBS Land general manager Fan Kow Hin said at a briefing on Saturday announcing the company's first half results.
"The rental market is expected to be soft and (will) probably be softer as more units become available," he said.
DBS Land expects up to 12,000 units will enter the market every year from 1997 to 1999.
"Supply in the next one to two years will be very large," Fan said, adding it may take up to 18 months for property prices to consolidate.
Company Deputy Chairman Cheng Fong said he does not expect a quick recovery in the property sector although steady economic growth should see the market mend over the next few years.
"With rising affordability and good economic growth, we should see prices firming up in a couple of years time," he said. "I don't think you'll see a further erosion of the market."

Fan said the property market should eventually recover and estimates up to 46,000 households living in public housing in Singapore have an income of S$8,000 and above and "can be considered for upgrading to the private market."
The property market has suffered a downturn after the government implemented measures to cool speculation last year.
